title: Why the 49th Parallel Became the Border #shorts
summary: The 49th parallel very roughly follows the northern edge of the Missouri basin acquired in the 1803 Louisiana Purchase; the 1818 Convention made it the boundary from the Lake of the Woods to the Rockies.
tags: why is the us canada border straight
sources: Convention of 1818, Article II: a line drawn from the most North Western Point of the Lake of the Woods along the forty Ninth Parallel of North Latitude ... from the Lake of the Woods to the Stony Mountains; signed London, 20 October 1818 (Avalon Project, Yale Law School): https://avalon.law.yale.edu/19th_century/conv1818.asp

1783 boundary to run due west from Lake of the Woods to the Mississippi, which rose farther south than shown on the Mitchell map (1755) the description rested on; the 49th parallel (1818) very roughly approximates the northern watershed of the Mississippi-Missouri drainage system of the Louisiana Territory, bought by the US from France in 1803; on the prairies the markers were mounds of sand or grass sod and later iron posts; in forest a vista is cut on each side of the line; the 1783 line ran by the St Croix, the St Lawrence, Lake Ontario, the Niagara, Lake Erie, Lake St Clair, Lake Huron and Lake Superior (The Canadian Encyclopedia, Boundaries): https://thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/boundaries

The first instance of a boundary drawn first on paper then traced on the ground; latitude determined with the zenith telescope (Talcott method) (American Society of Civil Engineers, Historic Civil Engineering Landmark: United States-Canadian Boundary Survey): https://www.asce.org/about-civil-engineering/history-and-heritage/historic-landmarks/united-states-canadian-boundary-survey

Map data: Natural Earth (public domain) https://www.naturalearthdata.com and US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain) https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/carto-boundary-file.html

scenes.narration: Why the {49th|forty-ninth} parallel? It very roughly follows the top of the Missouri River's basin: land the US bought in {1803|eighteen-oh-three}.
In {1818|eighteen eighteen}, that line became the border, from the Lake of the Woods to the Rockies.
And to find a parallel, you don't need to know the land. Just the stars.
